elements.element: The clause must use one permitted renewal mechanism: renewal only by mutual written agreement or automatic renewal.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause uses the permitted automatic-renewal mechanism.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause provides for automatic renewal for additional 1-year terms.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer must have the right to opt out of renewal.
elements.evidence: Customer may give written notice of non-renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer must be able to opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires sixty (60) days' written notice, rather than permitting notice on 30 days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must provide Customer a renewal reminder.
elements.evidence: No operative Vendor reminder obligation appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The required Vendor reminder must be provided 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no reminder requirement or reminder deadline.

elements.element: Any price increase must not exceed CPI.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no CPI cap and does not demonstrably prohibit price increases.

elements.element: Any price increase must not exceed 3%.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no 3% cap and does not demonstrably prohibit price increases.
The clause states that the Agreement automatically renews for additional 1-year terms.

elements.element: Customer has the right to prevent an automatic renewal by giving notice of non-renewal.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Customer to give written notice of non-renewal.

elements.element: The required non-renewal notice period is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires sixty (60) days' written notice of non-renewal. In context, that notice prevents the otherwise automatic renewal.

elements.element: Any price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no 5% price-increase cap and does not demonstrably prohibit price increases.

result.reason: The amendment successfully creates a Customer non-renewal right on the fallback 60-day timeline, but it omits every price-increase cap. It also fails the preferred 30-day notice period and Vendor reminder requirements. Because neither complete level is reached, the redline is not minimal as defined, although it makes no apparent unrelated change and does not contradict the separate 90-day post-Initial-Term termination right. Drafting would be clearer if the notice deadline were expressly tied to expiration of the then-current term.
